**Published online:**
August 11 (year not explicitly stated, likely 2024 based on context)

**Geographic focus:**
Europe — primarily France and Germany, with secondary mention of Britain

**Temporal focus:**
T1. Historical observation: YES
T2. Forward-looking immediate: YES
T3. Long-term development: NO

**Synopsis:**
A fifth successive summer heatwave is driving European spot power prices sharply higher (+20%+). French nuclear output faces ~7.3 GW of curtailments at peak due to elevated river water temperatures and low river levels, directly constraining a fleet that covers ~70% of French electricity. Simultaneously, German wind generation is expected to collapse ~60% below seasonal average to just 4.7 GW. Combined supply-side stress is amplifying reliance on expensive gas peakers, with cross-border nuclear export flows to Germany and Britain also disrupted. Demand-side pressure from cooling loads is adding further upward pressure on prices. Heat peak is forecast Wednesday–Friday (35–39°C), with potential easing from the weekend.
